sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in Maryville, TN?
sections.html:
A Maryville owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash offer for the house as it stands. The better choice turns on repair costs, timing and how much hassle you want to avoid.

Maryville is a smaller, steadier market than the cities around Nashville. The Census Bureau shows 32,442 residents in July 2025, only 1.7% above the 2020 base. Two thirds of homes (67.5%) are owner-occupied, the median value is $358,100, and 90.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Low turnover means many Maryville houses have long-term owners, and some of those houses have not been updated in decades.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good condition and you can wait for the right buyer.
  • Sell on your own if you are comfortable handling the contract and closing papers.
  • Take a cash offer when repairs, a tenant or an estate make a traditional sale harder.

Maryville is the seat of Blount County, set in the foothills of the Great Smoky Mountains, and its twin city Alcoa lies to the north. Wikipedia records that John Craig built Fort Craig here in 1785 and that the town was incorporated in 1795 and named for Mary Grainger Blount, wife of the territorial governor. Maryville College sits in town, and Chilhowee Mountain rises to the south.

The main routes are Broadway (U.S. 411 and 129), Lamar Alexander Parkway (U.S. 321, toward Townsend and the national park) and the Maryville-Alcoa Bypass toward Knoxville. Interstate 140 connects the area to McGhee Tyson Airport and West Knoxville. The Census Bureau's mean commute for workers is 23.3 minutes. Parks include the Bicentennial Greenbelt Park, the Maryville Alcoa Greenway and Sandy Springs Park.

sections.h2: What jobs and schools support Maryville home values?
sections.html:
The city's 2025 audit report names Denso Manufacturing Tennessee as the largest employer, with about 5,000 full-time employees since 1988, and Blount Memorial Hospital as the county's third largest at more than 2,700. Smith and Wesson headquarters, two Amazon locations and a BJ's Wholesale Club have added jobs more recently.

Maryville City Schools serves 5,619 students in eight schools, according to the same report, and the city put $9,422,500 from its general fund into school operations in fiscal 2025. The Census Bureau reports 93.7% of adults hold a high school diploma and 38.5% have a bachelor's degree or more, with a poverty rate of 6.7% and median household income of $81,963.

sections.h2: How do Maryville city and Blount County taxes work?
sections.html:
A Maryville house carries a city bill and a Blount County bill. The county rate fell to $1.29 per $100 of assessed value for 2026 from $1.59 in the three prior years, per the Blount County Trustee. The city's fiscal 2027 budget ordinance, on second reading in June 2026, funds the general fund at $1.36 per $100.

The Trustee's example makes the math concrete: a $250,000 house is assessed at $62,500, which produces a $806 county bill at the $1.29 rate. The official tax roll reflects the owner as of January 1, and the Trustee notes that taxes are normally prorated at closing with the buyer made the responsible party. Call the Trustee at 865-273-5900 or the City of Maryville financial services office at 865-273-3456 for payoff figures.

sections.h2: What building codes and permits matter when selling in Maryville?
sections.html:
Maryville Codes Enforcement, at 416 West Broadway, administers building and property maintenance rules and takes calls at 865-273-3500. According to the city's codes page, the council adopted the 2024 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Energy Conservation, Plumbing and Fire codes plus a 2024 Property Maintenance Code, all effective January 1, 2026. The 2017 National Electrical Code stays in force.

Any renovation done on or after that date falls under the new codes, so a buyer's contractor may ask for permits on recent work. The city also adopted tougher penalties for construction and property maintenance violations under state law. If you remodeled without a permit, talk to the codes office before listing.

It does, with a city permit and a safety check. The zoning code defines a short-term rental unit as a residential dwelling rented for less than 30 continuous days, and council held a public hearing in October 2019 on standards for these units under Section 14-211(29).

  • The application includes a sketch of the lot and floor plan showing bedrooms, beds, off-street parking and life safety equipment.
  • The owner swears an affidavit of life safety compliance covering UL 217 smoke alarms in and near each sleeping room and on each story, a carbon monoxide detector within 15 feet of bedrooms and a working fire extinguisher.
  • The equipment is subject to inspection before the permit is issued and afterward on reasonable notice.

If you are selling a short-term rental, tell the buyer which permit applies and call the planning office at 865-273-3500 about whether it transfers.

sections.h2: How does recording a deed work in Blount County?
sections.html:
Maryville deeds are filed with the Blount County Register of Deeds at 349 Court Street, phone 865-273-5880. The county's fee page lists a $12 recording charge for one or two pages, $5 for each added page and a $1 clerk fee, plus the state deed transfer tax of $0.37 per $100.

The office requires the district, map and parcel numbers on every deed, along with the responsible taxpayer's name and address. Trust deeds and mortgages must carry the statement of maximum principal indebtedness for recording tax purposes. Originals are returned after recording if you include a stamped return envelope.

One local quirk is worth knowing. Maryville has more than 250 old platted alleys, and the city is closing the ones no longer needed. When an alley closes it usually reverts 50/50 to the owners on each side, and the city prepares quitclaim deeds for them at no cost and records them. If your lot touches a platted alley, ask planning whether it has been abandoned.

faqs.q: Do I pay both city and county property tax on a Maryville house?
faqs.a: Yes. A house inside the city is billed by the City of Maryville and by Blount County, and each has its own rate. Ask both offices for a payoff before closing.

faqs.q: When are Blount County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices are mailed in early to mid-September and payable through the end of February. Taxes become delinquent on March 1, and 1.5% interest is added each month until paid.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Blount County taxes early?
faqs.a: Yes. The county gives 2% off for payment through October and 1% for November, and the discount is already shown on the notice.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Blount County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $12 for one or two pages plus $5 for each added page and a $1 clerk fee, and the state transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the price. The Register of Deeds can confirm the total for your document.

faqs.q: Who do I call about codes or permits in Maryville?
faqs.a: Call Maryville Codes Enforcement at 865-273-3500, at the Municipal Center, 416 West Broadway. Plan review and permits run through the same office.
